draft.title: Juxtaposition and contrast
card: Juxtaposition means placing two different things side by side. The writer puts them close together so the reader notices both at once.
Each thing makes the other stand out. A glittering party next to an empty street makes the party look brighter and the street look barer.
The reader is pushed to compare the two and ask why the writer set them together. This can bring out an idea, such as the gap between rich and poor.
To write about it, name the two things, say what is different about them, then explain the idea the comparison shows.
draft.remember: Two different things placed side by side, so each stands out and an idea becomes clear.

a.q: A writer describes a mansion with gold taps, then a tent in a park a few lines later. What is the effect of placing them together?
opts: Each stands out more, showing the gap between them
The mansion is made to seem less real than the tent
The reader is told how the narrator feels about both
The tent is shown to be the cause of the mansion
a.why: Putting the two close together makes the reader compare them, so wealth and hardship each stand out more. The option about the narrator's feelings is tempting, but juxtaposition works by the placing of things, not by stating feelings.
a.clue: Think about what the reader does when two different things sit close together.

b.q: In a short story, Leila sits in a bright, noisy classroom, then walks home to a silent, dark flat. Which sentence best explains the writer's purpose in placing these scenes together?
opts: To show how lonely home feels compared with school
To show that school is a more dangerous place
To show that the flat is the cause of the noise
To show that Leila dislikes every kind of noise
b.why: The bright, noisy classroom and the silent, dark flat are opposites, and placing them together makes her loneliness at home stand out. Saying she dislikes all noise is tempting, but the contrast points to the flat feeling empty, not to noise being unwanted.
b.clue: Look at what is different between the two places.

a.best: Each stands out more, showing the gap between them

b.best: To show how lonely home feels compared with school
